title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 113: The Vanilla Orchid: From Mesoamerica to Global Spice
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 113 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Vanilla Orchid: From Mesoamerica to Global Spice

Paragraph 1. Vanilla is the second most expensive spice in the world, right after saffron. People love its sweet smell in cakes and ice cream. The vanilla plant is a climbing orchid from the wet rainforests of Mexico. Hundreds of years ago, the Totonac people grew it in secret. Later, the Aztec rulers took the land and made the Totonacs pay vanilla as a tax. The Aztecs mixed vanilla into a special royal drink made with honey, corn, and crushed cacao beans.

Paragraph 2. After 1519, Spanish explorers carried vanilla pods across the ocean to Europe. Rich people in Europe loved the smell and tried to grow the plant in warm glass houses. The green plants grew big and made yellow flowers, but for three hundred years they never produced a single vanilla bean. Scientists found out why: inside the flower, a thin wall keeps the male pollen away from the female part. In Mexico, small stingless bees and tiny birds moved the pollen. Europe did not have those helpful animals.

Paragraph 3. In 1841, a twelve-year-old boy named Edmond Albius solved the puzzle on Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean. He used a thin stick of bamboo and his thumb to lift the flower wall and push the pollen inside by hand. This quick method took only a few seconds per flower. Soon, farmers on the nearby island of Madagascar learned the trick and became the world's largest seller of natural vanilla.

Paragraph 4. Even today, growing real vanilla needs huge human work. Each flower opens in the morning and dies by noon, so farm workers must pollinate every flower by hand early in the day. After that, the green pods grow for nine months and need months of drying in the sun to get their sweet smell. Because real vanilla takes so much work, over ninety-nine percent of modern vanilla foods use cheap artificial flavor made from oil or wood.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...made with honey, corn, and crushed cacao beans."
Đoạn 2: "...small stingless bees and tiny birds moved the pollen..."
Đoạn 3: "He used a thin stick of bamboo and his thumb..."
Đoạn 4: "...cheap artificial flavor made from oil or wood."

q5.text: Vanilla is currently the most expensive spice in the world.

steps: Đoạn 1: Vani là gia vị đắt thứ hai (second most expensive), đứng sau nghệ tây (saffron).

q6.text: European gardeners easily produced thousands of vanilla beans in the 1600s.

steps: Đoạn 2: Suốt 300 năm ở châu Âu, cây không tạo nổi một quả đậu nào (never produced a single vanilla bean).

q7.text: Edmond Albius invented a hand method to pollinate vanilla flowers when he was a boy.

steps: Đoạn 3: Edmond Albius tìm ra cách thụ phấn bằng tay khi mới 12 tuổi (twelve-year-old boy).

q8.text: Edmond Albius moved to Madagascar to teach farmers his new method.

steps: Đoạn 3: Chỉ nói nông dân Madagascar học được mẹo này, không hề nói Edmond Albius có chuyển sang Madagascar hay không.
